issues.issue: The grant of the right to transport oil and gas "from the subject and other lands" across the leasehold, surviving the term, conflicts with paragraph 25, under which the Lessee agrees not to assert that right unless the lands are pooled. A court would have to choose between the grant and the undertaking.

The term continues so long as gas is "produced or capable of being produced ... in paying quantities, in the judgment of the Lessee"; "paying quantities" is undefined and the Lessee's subjective judgment as the measure admits of competing readings.

The clause extends the term "as provided in Paragraph 7 following," but Paragraph 7 concerns adequacy of consideration and drilling discretion; the shut-in provision that bears on holding the lease is Paragraph 6. The cross-reference does not fit the paragraph invoked.
"A well shall be deemed commenced when preparations for drilling have been commenced" leaves "preparations for drilling" undefined, so almost any preliminary activity could satisfy it.

Addendum paragraph 16 defines commencement of operations as entry with equipment to build access roads followed by a drilling rig for spudding, a narrower test which the Addendum priority clause makes prevail. The two definitions conflict.

Royalty under (B) is one-eighth of "the price paid to Lessee," followed by struck-through language permitting deduction of post-production costs; whether the deletion prohibits such deductions is exactly the point on which the parties would divide. Subparagraph (A)'s "free of cost" and (C)'s mandatory tax deduction add further tension inside the same paragraph.

The clause fixes a shut-in payment but never says the payment keeps the lease alive, a gap that must be read with paragraph 2's habendum requiring production in paying quantities or capability of production. Whether shut-in payments hold the lease is left open.

This paragraph reserves "the further right of drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect," while paragraph 8 states the Lessee "shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres" in a unit. Both cannot be given unqualified effect.

"Lessee shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres contained in such unit" can be read as an affirmative obligation to drill or merely as a constraint on unit formation, and "maintain" fixes no time for compliance. The sentence sits in a clause that otherwise confers rights on the Lessee.

The density requirement stands against paragraph 7's reservation of the right of "drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect" and paragraph 20's bar on reading implied obligations into the lease. Whether it creates a development duty is a live question.

The Lessor's waiver of "notice of any assignment or transfer of the within lease" conflicts with Addendum paragraph 17, which requires the Lessee to give written notice of any assignment of a 51% or greater interest within fourteen days, the Addendum being stated to prevail.

"Any damages if not mutually agreed upon" go to three appraisers and "Arbitration shall be mandatory," but only crop and drainage damages are enumerated, so the reach of the catch-all and the character of the process as an arbitration are undefined.

The Lessor must abide by "all reasonable safety policies of Lessee ... including but not limited to" a single enumerated setback, leaving the catch-all's reach beyond that specific undefined and set unilaterally by the Lessee.

On surrender "the land rental hereinbefore set forth" is reduced in proportion to the acreage surrendered, but paragraph 3 makes this a "paid up bonus lease" and no land rental is set forth anywhere in the instrument. The reduction has nothing to operate on.

"Force majeure, including but not limited to acts of God, strikes, riots and governmental restrictions" leaves the catch-all's reach beyond the enumerated events undefined, and whether the lease is extended only ninety days after the event ends is ambiguous.

The Lessee need only "meet or commence to meet all or any part of the breaches alleged" within thirty days, which does not say what discharges the condition precedent to suit. Whether merely commencing suffices is open to argument.

The extension payment is to be tendered "in the same manner as provided in Paragraph numbered 6 hereof with regard to the method of payment of shut-in royalties," yet paragraph 6 sets the shut-in rate while paragraph 5 prescribes the method of payment. The cross-reference points to the wrong paragraph.

The bar on reading any "implied covenant, agreement or obligation" into the lease must be reconciled with paragraph 8's express well-density requirement and with the incorporated Addendum, which supersedes inconsistent main-body terms. The scope of the disclaimer is contestable.

This paragraph and Addendum paragraph 13 govern the same Clean and Green liability in different terms, the Addendum adding CREP and confining the trigger to operations on the Lessor's lands. Which text controls falls to the Addendum priority clause.

Locations are to be fixed by "mutual consent" with the Lessor's consent not unreasonably withheld, whereas Addendum paragraph 3 deems approval given if the Lessor fails to return the approval form within thirty days. The two consent regimes differ.

The undertaking not to assert a right to transport gas from other lands unless the premises are pooled contradicts paragraph 1's grant of that transport right "regardless of the source of such production," which is expressly to survive the lease term.

The clause operates only on an "inconsistency" with the main body, and several candidates exist — Addendum paragraph 16 against paragraph 3, Addendum paragraph 17 against paragraph 11's notice waiver, Addendum paragraph 8 against paragraph 1's injection and storage grant. Identifying inconsistency is itself the construction exercise.

Restoration "as nearly as possible" to the pre-drilling condition "within 90 days, weather permitting" states neither a measurable standard nor a firm deadline. Both are open-ended on the face of the clause.

"As near its original condition as is reasonably possible" is a looser and differently worded standard than Addendum paragraph 1's "as nearly as possible," and it carries no completion date. Which standard governs the same restoration work is unclear.

Deemed approval by thirty days' silence is hard to reconcile with main-body paragraph 23, which requires drilling sites, roads and pipelines to be located by "mutual consent" of Lessor and Lessee. Whether silence supplies that consent would have to be construed.

The indemnity survives only as fragments, so its operative promise, its beneficiary and the claims covered cannot be read from the text. What was agreed is not ascertainable on the face of the provision.

The covenant that the Lessee acquires no right to drill an underground gas or oil storage well conflicts with paragraph 1's grant of the right of "injecting and storing, air, gas, brine and other substances from any source and into any subsurface strata." The line between the two is contestable.

The trigger is a "material adverse change in the quality of Lessor's water supply" "during or immediately after the completion" of drilling; neither the materiality threshold nor the temporal window is defined. Both would have to be construed before the clause could be applied.

This paragraph and main-body paragraph 21 cover the same Clean and Green liability in different terms, the Addendum adding CREP and limiting the trigger to operations on the Lessor's lands. Which formulation governs turns on the Addendum priority clause.

The provision survives only as a fragment about responsibility for "any increase in property taxes, if any, levied upon Lessor," broken off mid-sentence, so the qualifying condition cannot be read. What increase is covered is not ascertainable from the text.
The audit right survives only in fragmentary form, so the scope of the audit, where it may be conducted and the notice required cannot be read off the text as printed.
